author: blu
body: Runtime GPT partition table reader and writer. Reads GPT headers and partition entries from disk via block-read-sector, writes new GPT partition tables via block-write-sector. Operates on live block devices, not compile-time buffers.

author: blu
body: So refuse the header rather than divide by what it says. This is the same rule fat16-parse-bpb already applies to bytes-per-sector, and for the same reason: a value that is about to be a divisor is checked before the arithmetic, not after it.

author: blu
body: Entries are packed four to a sector and the sector is written when the fourth lands. A partition count that is not a multiple of four therefore leaves the last few entries sitting in the buffer, and the zero-fill that follows stepped straight over that sector to the next boundary -- so the buffer was discarded and the entries never reached the disk.

author: blu
body: The fix is the flush: when the real entries run out mid-sector, write what is in the buffer before moving on. The tail of that sector is already zero, because the buffer is zeroed at the start of each sector.

author: blu
body: Answers the FIRST partition carrying a given type GUID, or None. A disk with two partitions of the same type is not an error here -- the caller decides what that means -- but for the fact store it is why the installer writes exactly one.
